components.note: 木 (wood) — the old sense was the ridgepole of a roof, the topmost point
及 (jí) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì jí hǎo.
example.english: The weather is extremely good today.
example.fact: 极 works as an adverb before an adjective (极好) or after one with 了: 好极了 (just great!). It also means a geographic or electrical pole: 南极, 北极, 阴极. 积极 (positive, active) and 极端 (extreme) are common compounds.

components.note: Simplified form of 蘭; the old plant radical on top has been reduced to two dots and a bar

example.hanzi: 她在窗台上养了一盆兰花。
example.pinyin: Tā zài chuāngtái shang yǎng le yì pén lánhuā.
example.english: She keeps a pot of orchids on the windowsill.
example.fact: 兰 is one of the 四君子 (four gentlemen) with plum, bamboo and chrysanthemum, all symbols of a refined person; orchids stand for modest elegance. It also appears in 荷兰 (the Netherlands), 兰州 and 爱尔兰 (Ireland).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — related to sound
向 (xiàng) gives the sound; xiǎng is close

example.pinyin: Diànhuà xiǎng le.
example.english: The phone rang.
example.fact: 响 is the verb for things that make a noise, such as phones, alarms and thunder: 手机响了, 雷声很响. It also forms 响亮 (loud and clear) and 影响 (influence, which literally means shadow and echo).

components.note: 尸 (body/roof) — a covered building
至 (zhì, to arrive) — the place where one arrives and stays

example.pinyin: Wūzi lǐ hěn nuǎnhuo.
example.english: It's warm in the room.
example.fact: 屋 is a bound form: spoken Chinese says 屋子 (room, especially in the north, where 里屋 means the inner room) or 房子 (house). 屋顶 is the roof, and the proverb 屋漏偏逢连夜雨 means that troubles come in clusters.

components.note: 目 (eye) — the old meaning of examining or looking closely
少 (shǎo) gives a rough sound hint for shěng

example.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng shěng diǎn qián.
example.english: I want to save a little money.
example.fact: 省 is shěng for saving (省钱, 省时间) and for a province (广东省), but xǐng in 反省 (to reflect on oneself). 省略 means to omit and 省事 means labour-saving.

components.note: 页 (head) — the top of the head
丁 (dīng) gives the sound; dǐng is close

example.pinyin: Shāndǐng shang hěn lěng.
example.english: It is cold on the mountain top.
example.fact: 顶 is both the highest point (山顶, 屋顶) and a measure word for hats and tents: 一顶帽子. As a verb it means to prop, to push against, or to talk back: 顶嘴.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — losing your way
米 (mǐ) gives the sound; mí is close

example.pinyin: Wǒ zài dà chéngshì lǐ mílù le.
example.english: I got lost in the big city.
example.fact: 迷 covers being lost (迷路) and being obsessed: 球迷 (football fan), 影迷 (film fan), 歌迷 (music fan). 迷信 means superstition and 着迷 means to be captivated.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — an old sense tied to bamboo; 'foolish' was a later extension
本 (běn) gives the sound; bèn is close

example.pinyin: Wǒ zhēn bèn, yòu wàng le dài yàoshi.
example.english: I'm so dumb, I forgot my keys again.
example.fact: 笨 means slow-witted or clumsy, milder than 傻 and often used in self-deprecation. It also describes bulk: 笨重 means heavy and awkward. The proverb 笨鸟先飞 (the slow bird flies first) praises extra effort.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a built structure
荅 (dá) gives a rough sound hint for tǎ

example.pinyin: Wǒmen pá shàng le nà zuò tǎ.
example.english: We climbed that tower.
example.fact: 塔 was coined to write the Sanskrit stupa that came with Buddhism, so Chinese pagodas are 塔. The measure word is 座. It now covers any tower: 铁塔, 电视塔, and 埃菲尔铁塔 (the Eiffel Tower).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — releasing or casting by hand
散 (sàn) means to scatter, which is the sense the hand action adds up to

example.pinyin: Tā cóng bù sāhuǎng.
example.english: He never tells lies.
example.fact: 撒 has two readings: sā (撒谎 to lie, 撒娇 to act coy, 撒手 to let go) and sǎ (to sprinkle, as in 撒盐). In 撒谎 the verb literally means "to cast a lie".

components.note: 火 (fire) — smoke comes from fire
因 (yīn) gives the sound; yān is close

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān chōu yì bāo yān.
example.english: He smokes a pack of cigarettes a day.
example.fact: 烟 means smoke and cigarettes: 抽烟 or 吸烟 (to smoke). Offering a cigarette (递烟) is a classic social gesture. 烟花 (fireworks) literally means smoke-flowers.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — shouting uses the mouth
咸 (xián) gives the sound; hǎn is close

example.pinyin: Tā zài ménkǒu hǎn wǒ de míngzi.
example.english: He called my name at the door.
example.fact: 喊 is to shout or call out for someone: 喊他过来 (call him over). It also means to address someone as: 喊他叔叔 (call him uncle). 喊口号 means to chant slogans.

components.note: 夂 (a foot coming down) — arrival or stepping
口 (mouth or dwelling) — the place a person arrives at

example.pinyin: Gèwèi tóngxué, qǐng zuò.
example.english: Everyone, please take a seat.
example.fact: 各 is a determiner placed before a noun: 各国 (every country), 各位 (everyone, polite), 各种 (all kinds). Compared with 每, 各 stresses that each member does its own thing: 各有各的想法.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — a supernatural being
麻 (má) gives the sound; mó is close

example.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ yǒu yí ge móguǐ.
example.english: There is a devil in the story.
example.fact: 魔 was created to write Sanskrit māra (the tempter) in Buddhist texts. It gives 魔法 (magic), 魔术 (conjuring), 魔鬼 (devil) and the slang 魔怔 (obsessed).

components.note: 龶 (plant sprout) — poison often came from plants
母 (mǔ) is the lower part and gives only a loose sound link

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng mógu yǒu dú.
example.english: This kind of mushroom is poisonous.
example.fact: 毒 covers poison and drugs: 有毒 (toxic), 吸毒 (to take drugs), 毒品 (narcotics). 病毒 (virus) is literally "illness poison". As an adjective it can mean cruel: 毒蛇 and 狠毒.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — a plant, here a wild weed
来 (lái) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Láiyīn Hé chuān guò hěn duō guójiā.
example.english: The Rhine flows through many countries.
example.fact: 莱 was an old word for a weedy plant, but today it mainly shows up in transliterations: 莱茵河 (the Rhine), 莱昂纳多 (Leonardo). 莱阳 is also a place famed for its pears.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — throwing by hand
率 (shuài) gives the sound; shuāi is close

example.hanzi: 他从自行车上摔下来了。
example.pinyin: Tā cóng zìxíngchē shang shuāi xiàlai le.
example.english: He fell off his bike.
example.fact: 摔 covers an accidental fall (摔倒) and a deliberate throw (摔东西, to smash things). It is more forceful than 掉. 摔跤 can mean either wrestling or a tumble.

components.note: 纟 (silk) — cutting a thread
色 (sè) gives only a loose sound hint for jué

example.pinyin: Tā jùjué le wǒ de yāoqǐng.
example.english: He turned down my invitation.
example.fact: 绝 originally meant to cut a thread. It gives 拒绝 (to refuse), 绝对 (absolutely), 绝望 (despair) and 绝种 (extinct). Slang 绝了 means "amazing", used as high praise.

components.note: Simplified form of 歸; the old shape had a woman and a broom, and the modern shape is a reduction of it

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì guī nǐ guǎn.
example.english: This matter is yours to handle.
example.fact: In modern speech 归 often means "to belong to / to be the responsibility of": 归你管, 这本书归我. In writing it means to return: 回归, 归还 (to give back), 归来 (to return home).

components.note: 手 (hand) — the hand closed into a fist
龹 (juàn) gives the sound and hints at curling fingers

example.pinyin: Tā wò jǐn le quántou.
example.english: He clenched his fist.
example.fact: 拳 is the fist, and also boxing or martial arts: 打拳, 太极拳. It is a measure word for punches: 打了他一拳 (punched him once).

components.note: Simplified form of 薩; the right-hand parts are a reduction and give no clue to sound or meaning

example.pinyin: Tā měitiān qù miào lǐ bài púsa.
example.english: She worships the Bodhisattva at the temple every day.
example.fact: 萨 appears almost only in 菩萨, from Sanskrit bodhisattva, and in transliterations like 萨克斯 (saxophone) and 萨摩亚 (Samoa). 菩萨心肠 means kind-hearted.

excludeSuggestion: Occurs almost only in 菩萨 and transliterated names

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and foundation
其 (qí) gives a rough sound hint for jī

example.pinyin: Zhè shì xuéxí Hànyǔ de jīchǔ.
example.english: This is the foundation of learning Chinese.
example.fact: 基 is a bound form meaning base: 基础 (foundation), 基本 (basic), 基地 (base), 基因 (gene). Several of the words use it together with 本 or 础, which also mean root or foundation.

meanings: measure word for bolts of cloth

components.note: Origin debated, often linked to a folded length of cloth, which fits its measure-word use

example.pinyin: Cǎodì shang yǒu sān pǐ mǎ.
example.english: There are three horses on the grass.
example.fact: 匹 is the measure word for horses and bolts of cloth: 一匹马, 一匹布. It also means to match: 匹配 (to pair up) and 匹敌 (to be a match for). 单枪匹马 describes someone going it alone.

components.note: A drawing of an animal's horn, with the curved tip and ridged body

example.pinyin: Niú yǒu liǎng zhī jiǎo.
example.english: A cow has two horns.
example.fact: 角 is jiǎo for horn, corner and angle: 三角形 (triangle), 墙角 (corner). It is jué in 角色 (role) and 主角 (lead). In money, 一角 is a tenth of a yuan, spoken as 毛.

components.note: 卩 (kneeling person) — a hand pressing a person down, usually taken as the old 'press' picture behind seals and prints

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè zhāng zhǐ yìn chūlai.
example.english: Please print this sheet out.
example.fact: 印 means to press a mark: 印章 (seal, chop), 印象 (impression), 印刷 (printing). The same shape names a seal of authority, which is why 盖印 (to stamp) makes a document official. In computing 打印 means to print.

components.note: Simplified from 東, usually explained as the sun rising behind a tree; the simplified shape no longer shows that picture

example.pinyin: Tàiyáng cóng dōngbian shēngqǐ.
example.english: The sun rises in the east.
example.fact: 东西 is dōngxī for "east and west" but dōngxi (neutral tone) for "thing", a famous pair. 房东 (landlord) and 东道主 (host) come from the idea of the host sitting on the east side.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — the old sense was going somewhere and reaching it
告 (gào) gives the sound; zào is close

example.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē shì zài Zhōngguó zào de.
example.english: This car was made in China.
example.fact: 造 is to make something, including abstractions: 造句 (to make a sentence), 造成 (to cause, used for bad results). It also forms 制造 (to manufacture), 创造 (to create) and 造型 (modelling, styling).

components.note: Origin unclear; the modern shape shows a topped piece over 巾, and its first meaning was the marketplace

example.pinyin: Wǒmen qù chāoshì mǎi cài.
example.english: We are going to the supermarket to buy groceries.
example.fact: 市 is a city and a market: 超市, 市场, 市民 (citizens). It also names the traditional "market" units, as in 市斤 (500 g), which is still used for shopping in China.

components.note: 纟 (silk) — a rope or cord
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound hint for wéi

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá fùzé wéichí zhìxù.
example.english: The police are responsible for keeping order.
example.fact: 维 began as a rope that holds things together, and it gives 维持 (to maintain), 维护 (to safeguard), 维修 (to repair) and 维生素 (vitamin). 三维 means three-dimensional and 思维 means thinking.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — the sickness radical
正 (zhèng) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìng de zhèngzhuàng hěn qīng.
example.english: The symptoms of this illness are mild.
example.fact: 症 is a bound form: 症状 (symptom), 炎症 (inflammation), 失眠症 (insomnia). 后遗症 means sequelae and is also used figuratively for side effects of a policy.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — the plant stem
帝 (dì) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Guā shú dì luò.
example.english: When the melon is ripe, the stem falls away.
example.fact: 瓜熟蒂落 is a proverb meaning that things happen naturally once conditions are right. 蒂 also forms 根深蒂固 (deeply rooted) and appears in transliterations like 蒂芙尼 (Tiffany).

excludeSuggestion: Bound form, found mainly in idioms and transliterated names

components.note: 心 (heart) — the mind asking how
乍 (zhà) gives the sound; zěn is close

example.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme qù xuéxiào?
example.english: How do you get to school?
example.fact: 怎 never appears alone: it is in 怎么 (how / why), 怎样 (how) and 怎么样 (how is it?). 怎么 can ask for a method (怎么去) or express surprise (你怎么来了, why are you here?).

components.note: 亻 (person) — people taking over from each other
弋 (yì) gives a loose sound hint for dài

example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ dài wǒ qù ma?
example.english: Can you go in my place?
example.fact: 代 means to substitute: 代替, 代表 (represent), and the polite 代我向他问好 (give him my regards). It also means generation or era: 现代, 年代, 下一代.

components.note: 癶 (two feet) — stepping up
豆 (dòu) was a stand or vessel one steps onto, and also gives a loose sound hint

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò qù dēngshān.
example.english: We are going mountain climbing this weekend.
example.fact: 登 is formal climbing (登山), boarding (登机) and entering information: 登录 (to log in). 登陆 is a homophone meaning to land or to come ashore, so both are dēnglù. 登报 means to publish in a newspaper.

components.note: 几 (a low stool) — a thing one leans on
任 (rèn) means to leave to or rely on, adding the idea of dependence

example.pinyin: Nǐ píng shénme zhèyàng shuō?
example.english: On what basis do you say that?
example.fact: 凭什么 means "on what grounds?" and is often a challenge. 凭 is also "to rely on": 凭票入场 (admission by ticket). It forms 文凭 (diploma) and 凭证 (voucher).

components.note: A cloud line with drops falling beneath it; it is also the radical for weather words such as 雪, 雷 and 云

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn xià yǔ le.
example.english: It's raining outside.
example.fact: Chinese says 下雨 ("rain falls"), and the measure word is 场 or 阵: 一场大雨. 雨伞 is an umbrella, and the 雨 radical heads many weather characters like 雪, 雷 and 雾.

components.note: 石 (stone) — a heavy weight, like a scale weight
旁 (páng) gives a rough sound hint for bàng

example.pinyin: Zhège bāo yǒu shí bàng zhòng.
example.english: This bag weighs ten pounds.
example.fact: 磅 is the weight pound (about 454 g), borrowed from English, while the currency pound uses a different character: 英镑. 磅秤 is a platform scale, and in 磅礴 (grand, majestic) it is read páng.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a spoken particle
各 (gè) gives the sound of the related reading gē

example.pinyin: Nà wǒmen zǒu lo.
example.english: Then let's go.
example.fact: 咯 is a casual sentence-final particle suggesting "so, that's how it is", softer than 了: 好咯, 对咯. The same character is also gē in 咯咯 (clucking, giggling).

excludeSuggestion: Informal sentence particle, often written 喽 or 啰 instead

components.note: 大 (big) — the old 奪 had a large bird figure
寸 (hand) — a hand holding it, from which the item escapes or is snatched away

example.pinyin: Tā duó dé le guànjūn.
example.english: He won the championship.
example.fact: 夺 means to take by force: 夺走 (to snatch), 夺取 (to seize). In sports news 夺冠 is shorthand for "to win the title". 夺目 means dazzling.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 租 first meant grain paid as a tax or rent
且 (qiě) gives a loose sound link for zū

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zū le yí tào gōngyù.
example.english: We rented an apartment.
example.fact: 租 works in both directions: 租房 (to rent a flat), 出租 (to rent out), 房租 (rent). 出租车 is a taxi, literally "for-rent car".

components.note: Simplified form of 傑; the modern 木 with four dots is a reduction, and the dots here are not fire

example.hanzi: 他是一位杰出的科学家。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi jiéchū de kēxuéjiā.
example.english: He is an outstanding scientist.
example.fact: 杰 is a bound form: 杰出 (outstanding), 杰作 (masterpiece), 豪杰 (hero). It is also a popular given name element, as in Jay Chou's Chinese name 周杰伦.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a type of person
老 (lǎo) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Tā shì ge dàlǎo.
example.english: He is a big shot.
example.fact: 佬 comes from southern and Cantonese speech as a casual suffix for men, as in 港佬 or 广东佬. 大佬 originally meant boss or elder brother in Cantonese. In mainland slang 大佬 now means an expert, e.g. 技术大佬.

meanings: measure word for articles and essays

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips on which early writing was recorded
扁 (biǎn) gives the sound; piān is close

example.hanzi: 我读了一篇有趣的文章。
example.pinyin: Wǒ dú le yì piān yǒuqù de wénzhāng.
example.english: I read an interesting article.
example.fact: 篇 is the measure word for complete written pieces: 一篇文章, 一篇作文, 一篇日记. The bamboo radical comes from the days when writing was done on strung bamboo slips.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 科 first meant grading grain
斗 (a measure for grain) — the container used for grading

example.pinyin: Tā zài yīyuàn de nèikē gōngzuò.
example.english: He works in the internal medicine department at the hospital.
example.fact: 科 is about categories: 内科 (internal medicine), 外科 (surgery), 科目 (subject), 科学 (science), 科长 (section chief). In biology, 科 is the taxonomic "family".

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a sound made with the mouth
亨 (hēng) gives the sound exactly

example.pinyin: Tā yìbiān zǒulù yìbiān hēng gē.
example.english: He hums a song as he walks.
example.fact: 哼 imitates a soft sound: 哼歌 (hum a tune), a snort of disdain (哼!) or a groan. In stories the "Heng and Ha" generals (哼哈二将) are guardian figures at temple gates.

components.note: 心 (heart) — thoughts and feelings
今 (jīn) gives a rough sound hint for niàn

example.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ niàn yíxià zhè jù huà.
example.english: Please read this sentence aloud.
example.fact: 念 means to read aloud (念课文) and to study (念大学, to attend university), both used colloquially. It also means to think of someone: 想念 (miss), 怀念 (cherish the memory of), 纪念 (to commemorate).

components.note: 纟 (silk) — a cord or rope
邦 (bāng) gives the sound; bǎng is close

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ xíngli bǎng jǐn.
example.english: Please tie the luggage down tightly.
example.fact: 绑 means to tie up firmly with a rope: 绑腿, 绑带. 绑架 is to kidnap. In apps 绑定 means to link an account, as in 绑定手机号 (link a phone number).

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a building being protected
寸 (hand) — a hand holding on to it

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá shǒu zài ménkǒu.
example.english: The police are standing guard at the door.
example.fact: 守 is to guard and to keep a promise or a rule: 守信, 守时 (to be punctual), 守规矩. 守岁 is the New Year's Eve custom of staying up late to welcome the new year.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — a spoken pledge
若 (ruò) gives the sound; nuò is close

example.pinyin: Tā shì ge yí nuò qiān jīn de rén.
example.english: He is a man whose word is his bond.
example.fact: 诺 is a bound form for promising: 承诺 (to commit), 诺言 (a promise), 一诺千金 (one promise worth a thousand gold). It also writes the first syllable of 诺贝尔 (Nobel).

components.note: 木 (tree) — doubled, a group of trees makes a wood

example.pinyin: Zhè piàn shùlín hěn dà.
example.english: This forest is very large.
example.fact: 林 is two 木 for a wood, and three 木 make 森 (sēn, dense forest). It is also one of the most common Chinese surnames (Lín), and 林 can mean any circle of people, as in 艺林 (art circles).
